{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the hxm_program hub's field report of 2026-09-28 (art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28), item O-19, in the reporter's words: "Evidence grades on checks. `measured-run` / `operator-attested (since, duration, who)` / `inferred`, plus a closure rule the owner sets: e.g. 'operator-attested for ≥ 7 days closes a stale check at grade B, and a real run upgrades it'. `loop_status` and `/where` would then say 'closed on operator evidence, not re-run' instead of 're-run owed' forever." The case: a data-path check that failed on 2026-09-10 was repaired on 2026-09-17 and has run in user operations for 11 days with no complaint.

WHAT IS MEASURED (fact:root-cause-a-stale-check-leaves-attention-only-by-its-own-run-and-other-evidence-cannot-answer-it-2026-09-28): operator evidence already has an honest home. A second check with method `observation`, kind `validation`, performed in a production Environment, clears the unproven-capability gap and shows in evidence_report as proven in production. What nothing does is let that evidence, or an owner's `parks` ruling, answer the STALE check. It leaves loop_status attention only if its own status becomes `passing` or `superseded`.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A GRADE ON THE RUN, as the reporter describes: an evidence-grade field (measured run / operator-attested with since, duration and who / inferred) on the check, read by every rollup, which then prints the grade beside the status.
(b) A RELATION BETWEEN CHECKS: the observation check ANSWERS the stale scripted check (a typed edge, or INVALIDATES-like with a grade). The stale check's row then reads "answered by operator evidence since 2026-09-17, not re-run", and a real run of the scripted check replaces the answer. There is no new field on Verification, and the operator evidence stays its own dated record.
(c) AN OWNER-SET CLOSURE RULE (the reporter's second half): a DesignRule or accepted Decision stating when weaker evidence may close a stale check ("operator-attested ≥ 7 days"). The loop reads it as it reads `parks` elsewhere, and says so on the row. This is a ruling, not an inference, and it builds on (a) or (b).
(d) TEACH WHAT EXISTS AND CHANGE NOTHING: the skills name the observation-check route. The stale check stays listed, and its row points at the observation check that proves the capability. Small, and it leaves "re-run owed" standing, which the reporter says reads as false debt to an operator.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· cap:a-repair-can-say-what-it-invalidated was built on purpose so that "a claim says a verdict is STALE, never that it has turned, and only a run can say what is true now". Any option that takes a stale check out of attention must stay honest to that: the row has to SAY it was closed at a lower grade, never read as a pass.
· "No complaint for 11 days" is absence of a report, and a quiet failure passes it. The grade has to carry that weakness, which is the reporter's own framing: "weaker than a re-run and much stronger than nothing".
· This is the THIRD shape of one class. qs (partly blocked, 2026-09-04) and dev_storyflow (expected change, 2026-09-25) are held in dec:idea-a-run-can-pass-with-its-exceptions-stated, and dec:idea-a-finding-carries-its-bounds proposes a `grade`. Settling any one alone risks three overlapping homes for a check's qualification on one node type.
